title: HALITI and OTHERS v. DENMARK
summary: In Haliti and Others v. Denmark, the applicants—Murat Haliti, Gjylperian Haliti, and their three children—are nationals of Serbia and Montenegro of Roma origin, represented by the European Roma Rights Centre. Their case against Denmark focused on the vulnerability of Roma and related groups facing persecution and harassment in Kosovo, particularly after the 1999 conflict, and the risk of inhuman or degrading treatment if returned. The Haliti family entered Denmark in July 2001, seeking asylum due to past violence, including a beating by the Kosovo Liberation Army and ongoing harassment and threats upon their return to Kosovo. Danish authorities denied their asylum claim, finding that the incidents described did not meet the threshold for persecution and that the general security situation in Kosovo, with international protection present, did not pose a concrete risk to them. The European Court of Human Rights examined their complaints under Articles 3 (prohibition of inhuman or degrading treatment), 13 (right to an effective remedy), and 14 (prohibition of discrimination), but declared the application inadmissible. The Court found no evidence of a real risk of ill-treatment upon return and noted that domestic remedies were still pending. This case highlights the ongoing challenges Roma and related communities face in seeking international protection, especially in the context of post-conflict Kosovo and evolving European asylum standards.
